articles.title: How to Remember What You Learn From Stack Overflow (Without Bookmarking Forever)
articles.excerpt: You've hit this exact bug before. CORS error on a refresh token. Or a CSS flex child that refuses to shrink. Or a JWT that works in Postman and dies in the browser. You open a new tab, type half the e…
articles.body: You've hit this exact bug before. CORS error on a refresh token. Or a CSS flex child that refuses to shrink. Or a JWT that works in Postman and dies in the browser. You open a new tab, type half the error message, and there it is: the same Stack Overflow answer you starred eight months ago, still sitting in a browser folder you never open. I used to call that "research." It was just forgetting with extra steps. Why bookmarks and stars don't teach you anything Starring an SO answer feels productive. Same with copying a snippet into a random notes file named fix.md or dumping the URL into a catch-all page titled "Debugging tips." You've captured the where . You haven't captured the why . Next time the bug shows up, your brain doesn't search fix.md . It searches Google.

articles.title: We Checked 61 Official MCP Servers Against the Auth Spec
articles.excerpt: Most SaaS companies now ship an official remote MCP server, and most of them sit behind OAuth. We wanted to know how closely those servers follow the current MCP authorization spec (the 2026-07-28 rev…
articles.body: Most SaaS companies now ship an official remote MCP server, and most of them sit behind OAuth. We wanted to know how closely those servers follow the current MCP authorization spec (the 2026-07-28 revision), so we checked the official servers of 67 vendors from the outside. 61 of them require a login. This post is about those 61. The short version: the basics are done everywhere. The newer parts of the spec are not. How we checked We used our free MCP Server Check . It is passive. For each server it sends one unauthenticated initialize request, reads the public OAuth discovery documents, and calls tools/list only if the server answers without a token. It never calls a tool and never sends a token. We ran every server on October 26 and again on November 4, 2026.

articles.body: 시력을 되돌리는 임플란트 승인 뉴스에서 시작해, 양안시 훈련의 도구를 다시 생각하다 안녕하세요, Seven Sportz 팀입니다. 이번 주에 눈에 띈 뉴스 하나로 시작하겠습니다. MIT Technology Review는 지도성 위축(geographic atrophy) 형태의 황반변성 환자에게 시각을 되돌려주는 이식형 시스템 PRIMA를 보도했습니다. 지난 7월 유럽에서 승인됐고, 미국 FDA 허가를 기다리는 중입니다. 전 세계 500만 명 이상이 이 형태의 AMD를 겪고 있고, 지금까지 이들에게 시력을 되돌려줄 치료는 없었습니다. 왜 이 이야기를 꺼내냐면, 저희가 매일 씨름하는 문제와 정확히 같은 뿌리를 가지고 있기 때문입니다. 시각은 뇌가 두 눈의 입력을 통합해서 만드는 결과물입니다. PRIMA는 망막 세포가 사라진 자리에 신호를 다시 넣는 방식으로 그 통합 과정에 개입합니다. 저희가 다루는 약시(lazy eye)는 그보다 훨씬 앞단의 문제입니다. 눈은 멀쩡한데, 뇌가 한쪽 눈의 입력을 무시하도록 학습해버린 상태죠. 그래서 약시 훈련의 목표는 약한 눈을 혼자 혹사시키는 게 아니라, 두 눈이 같이 일하도록 뇌를 다시 설득하는 쪽으로 옮겨갑니다. 디콥틱(dichoptic) 접근이라고 부릅니다. 왜 안대로는 안 되는가 안대는 원리가 명확합니다. 우세안을 가리면 약시안이 강제로 일하게 되니까요. 하지만 지속성이 나쁩니다. 아이는 불편해하고, 성인은 시작할 기회조차 없습니다. 무엇보다 안대는 양안 상호작용을 아예 차단합니다. 뇌가 두 눈을 함께 쓰는 법을 배우려면, 두 눈에 동시에 다른 자극을 줘야 합니다.

articles.title: Cheap Metrics Dashboards for Checkout Failures — Prometheus and Grafana in Python
articles.excerpt: For a small e-commerce team, Prometheus and Grafana are the best default for a free checkout-failure dashboard. Prometheus collects the time series; Grafana turns them into a useful, dynamic view, and…
articles.body: For a small e-commerce team, Prometheus and Grafana are the best default for a free checkout-failure dashboard. Prometheus collects the time series; Grafana turns them into a useful, dynamic view, and both can be self-hosted. The important design choice is not the dashboard theme. It is the cost dimension attached to each failure. I would start with a few stable metrics: checkout attempts, failed checkouts, payment-provider failures, and estimated order value at risk. Then I would add a label for the service or provider that owns the failure. That gives the team a way to ask, “Which part of checkout is creating the most operational and business cost?” without putting every raw event into a spreadsheet. Should a small team choose cheap or free metrics dashboard software?

articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope is healthy but is being pulled down toward Earth by atmospheric drag. NASA is considering options to extend the iconic telescope's work.
articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency , was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.body: The three Americans currently living off Earth just made sure their electoral voices were heard. Anil Menon told us today (Nov. 3) that he and fellow NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins voted in the U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station (ISS). "Yes, you can even vote from space! All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials," Menon wrote in an X post this morning . Yes, you can even vote from space! All three US crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials.

articles.excerpt: The OG sci-fi browser game is still going strong.
articles.body: If you were on the Internet in the early 2000s looking for free browser games to play, OGame was a blooming sci-fi strategy sensation that couldn't be ignored. With online servers providing the structure for a living and evolving universe where players fought, traded, and created empires from scratch, its limited visual presentation was no issue. Times have changed, but GameForge hasn't gone anywhere. OGame has been ported to mobile devices, and content updates have kept it alive and fresh for much longer than a plethora of installable MMO games.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .

articles.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
articles.excerpt: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail formed when two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together.
articles.body: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old.
